chunks: And from Ibn Abi Khaythama who said: Affan and Yahya ibn Ishaq as-Saylaheeni narrated to us, they said: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn Uthman narrated from Abut-Tufayl, who said: Abdullah ibn Amr said:

"O Abut-Tufayl, count twelve from the sons of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay, then comes al-Naqf and an-Naqaf." The narrations on this meaning from the paths of the general public (Sunni) are numerous, indicating that the Messenger of Allah mentioned the twelve and that they are his successors.

key_terms.النَّقْفُ وَالنَّقَاف: Al-Naqf and an-Naqaf (periods of fighting and killing)
key_terms.الْعَامَّة: The general public (referring to Sunni Muslims)
key_terms.بَنِي كَعْبِ بْنِ لُؤَي: Sons of Ka'b ibn Lu'ay (a lineage of Quraysh)

ai.seo_question: What do the terms al-Naqf and an-Naqaf signify in the context of the twelve successors?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Sunni consensus on the 'Twelve Caliphs' (Al-Arba'ah al-Ashraf), linking their succession to the subsequent era of conflict known as 'al-Naqf and an-Naqaf.' Al-Nu'mani includes this to demonstrate that the concept of twelve specific successors is rooted in early Prophetic tradition, serving as a foundational proof for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams in Shia theology.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (27) Ibn Abu Khaythama narrated from Affan and Yahya bin Iss’haq as-Saylaheeni from Hammad bin Salama from Abdullah bin Uthman from Abut-Tufayl that Abdullah bin Amr had said to him:

“O Abut-Tufayl, count twelve ones from bani Ka’b bin Lu’ay and then fighting and killing occur.” The traditions narrated by the Sunni concerning this subject are so many. They confirm that the Prophet (S) has mentioned twelve men to be the caliphs after him.
